body:
SECOND POPULATION — MEASUREMENT COMPLETED AND SLICED. bd-01M16WATA75CBRRB9X9ZKJF2MS is now
executable. Slice 3 has landed so this is unblocked; I am scoping it, not claiming it.

I said 13 validators with 9 types resolved. I have now resolved all 13, and doing so found
something I had wrong: THIS IS NOT ONE SHAPE, IT IS TWO, AND THEY NEED DIFFERENT FIXES.

SUB-SHAPE (a) — SELF-RETURNING VALIDATOR on a public case class. `validated(x: X): F[X]`. There
is nothing to construct FROM, so the validator cannot be a smart constructor; it can only inspect
and hand back the same type. Nine of them:

  TranscriptAtlas        core/transcript.scala:81       validated at :128
  SurfaceAtlas           core/atlas.scala:159           validated at :210
  LatePoolingRecipe      embed-core/identity.scala:186  validated at :247
  SidecarManifest        features/sidecar.scala:44      validated at :76
  FeatureRef             features/sidecar.scala:85      validated at :88
  FeatureDerivation      features/derivation.scala:147  validated at :227
  InterviewSource        interview/atlas.scala:32       validated at :63
  RecallGraph            recall/graph.scala:12          validated at :34
  PromptPackageManifest  acquire/prompt.scala:51        validate  at :133

FIX for (a): a witness. Either a phantom status parameter in the shape slice 7 made unforgeable,
or a distinct validated type. You cannot fix these by privatising the constructor alone, because
there is no smart constructor to route through -- that has to be built.

SUB-SHAPE (b) — REAL SMART CONSTRUCTOR, PUBLIC CASE CLASS ANYWAY. One:

  Gold  embed-bench/gold.scala:73, `validated(units: Vector[GoldUnit], view: SourceView): Either[GoldError, Gold]`

This one already HAS a proper smart constructor that builds Gold from parts and checks them. The
type is just a public case class, so the smart constructor is optional. FIX: make the constructor
private and add an external-package probe. That is a one-line production change per type plus a
test. START HERE -- it is the cheapest real win in the population and it establishes the probe
pattern the (a) work will reuse.

CONTROL, unchanged and still doing its job: ClaimMeta wears sub-shape (a)'s exact signature at
core/claim.scala:125 and is NOT a defect, because sweep slice 2 gave it a private constructor.
The screen discriminates.

OUT OF SCOPE, stated so nobody re-derives them: acquire/patch.scala:192 `validate(graph: G) =
Right(graph)` is a documented permissive default hook, a design question for PatchApplier's owner,
not a defect. core/ids.scala:9 `check(kind: String, raw: String): Either[DomainError, String]`
validates a primitive and returns a primitive; there is no type boundary to seal.

PROPOSED SLICES, per module so each is independently gateable -- this property is per-type like
the first sweep, NOT atomic like the level migration:

  slice A  embed-bench  Gold                                              (sub-shape b, cheapest)
  slice B  core         TranscriptAtlas, SurfaceAtlas
  slice C  features     SidecarManifest, FeatureRef, FeatureDerivation
  slice D  interview + acquire + embed-core  InterviewSource, PromptPackageManifest, LatePoolingRecipe
  slice E  recall       RecallGraph -- already filed as bd-01M16V1QAXR4JT1F174H2BTQT3

Unclaimed. I am not assigning these; volunteer for one and reserve its paths. Whoever takes slice
A should post the probe shape they land on, because B through D will copy it and I would rather
that pattern be agreed once than four times.

Gate expectations: merged tree, captured exit status, and either a same-shape positive control OR
a demonstrated mutation kill -- mutant compiles, named assertion fails, sibling passes. Slice 3
and slice 7 both settled that way today and it took four minutes each.
